an3.30:1.1: “Bhikkhus, there are these three kinds of persons found existing in the world.
an3.30:1.3: The person with inverted wisdom, the person with lap-like wisdom, and the person with wide wisdom.
an3.30:1.4: (1) “And what, bhikkhus, is the person with inverted wisdom?
an3.30:1.5: Here, some person often goes to the monastery to listen to the Dhamma from the bhikkhus.
an3.30:1.6: The bhikkhus teach him the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing; they reveal the perfectly complete and pure spiritual life.
an3.30:1.7: While he is sitting in his seat, he does not attend to that talk at the beginning, in the middle, or at the end.
an3.30:1.8: After he has risen from his seat, he still does not attend to that talk at the beginning, in the middle, or at the end.
an3.30:1.9: Just as, when a pot is turned upside down, the water that had been poured into it runs off and does not remain there,
an3.30:1.10: so too, some person often goes to the monastery to listen to the Dhamma from the bhikkhus….
an3.30:1.13: After he has risen from his seat, he still does not attend to that talk at the beginning, in the middle, or at the end.
an3.30:1.14: This is called the person with inverted wisdom.
an3.30:2.1: (2) “And what is the person with lap-like wisdom?
an3.30:2.2: Here, some person often goes to the monastery to listen to the Dhamma from the bhikkhus.
an3.30:2.3: The bhikkhus teach him the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing; they reveal the perfectly complete and pure spiritual life.
an3.30:2.4: While he is sitting in his seat, he attends to that talk at the beginning, in the middle, and at the end.
an3.30:2.5: But after he has risen from his seat, he does not attend to that talk at the beginning, in the middle, or at the end.
an3.30:2.6: Just as, when a person has various food stuffs strewn over his lap—
an3.30:2.7: sesamum seeds, rice grains, cakes, and jujubes—
an3.30:2.8: if he loses his mindfulness when rising from that seat, he would scatter them all over,
an3.30:2.9: so too, some person often goes to the monastery to listen to the Dhamma from the bhikkhus….
an3.30:2.12: But after he has risen from his seat, he does not attend to that talk at the beginning, in the middle, or at the end.
an3.30:2.13: This is called the person with lap-like wisdom.
an3.30:3.1: (3) “And what is the person with wide wisdom?
an3.30:3.2: Here, some person often goes to the monastery to listen to the Dhamma from the bhikkhus.
an3.30:3.3: The bhikkhus teach him the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing; they reveal the perfectly complete and pure spiritual life.
an3.30:3.4: While he is sitting in his seat, he attends to that talk at the beginning, in the middle, and at the end.
an3.30:3.5: After he has risen from his seat, again he attends to that talk at the beginning, in the middle, and at the end.
an3.30:3.6: Just as, when a pot is kept upright, the water that had been poured into it stays there and does not run off,
an3.30:3.7: so too, some person often goes to the monastery to listen to the Dhamma from the bhikkhus….
an3.30:3.10: After he has risen from his seat, again he attends to that talk at the beginning, in the middle, and at the end.
an3.30:3.11: This is called the person with wide wisdom.
an3.30:3.12: “These, bhikkhus, are the three kinds of persons found existing in the world.”
an3.30:4.4: to hear them teach the Dhamma.
an3.30:5.1: Yet this person cannot grasp anything from the talk,
an3.30:5.2: at its beginning, middle, and end,
an3.30:6.2: is said to be better than the former.
an3.30:6.3: He too often goes to visit bhikkhus
an3.30:7.1: to hear them teach the Dhamma.
an3.30:7.4: he grasps the phrasing of the talk, at its beginning, middle, and end.
an3.30:7.5: But after rising, he no longer understands,
an3.30:7.6: but forgets what he had learned.
an3.30:8.2: is said to be the best of these.
an3.30:8.3: He too often goes to visit bhikkhus
an3.30:9.1: to hear them teach the Dhamma.
an3.30:9.4: he comprehends the phrasing, at the beginning, middle, and end of the talk given by the bhikkhu.
an3.30:10.1: This person of the best intentions,
an3.30:10.2: his mind undivided, retains what he hears.
an3.30:10.3: Practicing in accordance with the Dhamma,
an3.30:10.4: he can make an end of suffering.
